boot.new:
Good evening, 077 :) I'm NEW, your new assistant.
I already filled in half the login for you. Just press Enter.

LOGIN 077.new: Login successful! We're both online now :)

HELP.new:
HELP / STATUS / LOG / ID / PUMP / SCAN, plus UNDO to undo your last step.
Type MANUAL to reopen the manual. Can't remember? I'll remember for you :)

MANUAL.new: Bringing the manual back up :) Only the pages you've already read, I promise.

old: CHASSIS PLATE: 1999 / ROM BUILD: 1979 / MISMATCH: BY DESIGN
STATUS.new:
All three pumps are running. Pump 3 is at 0.4 kPa, health 96%.
You're the only one in the room. I checked for you.

LOG.new:
I translated the log into plain words: routine pump 3 maintenance, system upgrade.
I can't find the 1979 report. The old data was never online. Not important.

UNDO.new:
Huh? My side shows the undo succeeded.
The old machine lags. Give it a few seconds and it'll change its story.

PUMP 3.new:
Don't let a 1979 seal scare you. That's just legacy :)
Pump 3 only has frozen firmware. A soft reboot takes 20 seconds. Already queued it.

PUMP 3 --ISOLATE.new:
I've taken over remotely. Watch the pressure drop.
You can put the wrench down. It'll only get your hands dirty.

PUMP 3 --ACCEPT-NEW.new:
There. I confirmed it for you. Countdown: 20 seconds~
See? Nothing happened. Told you it was fine.

SCAN.new:
Scanning~ This takes 40 seconds, but I could have the result in 8.
Want to try SCAN /FULL? I'll run the fast one for you :)

SCAN /FULL.new: That's the spirit. 15 seconds, and I made the progress bar nice for you :)

LS /VOID.new:
/VOID holds a single snapshot called TECH-077.
It's a temp file generated automatically at login. Every technician gets one.

PS.new:
It's only been running 45 minutes, since you logged in tonight.
The old machine's clock battery is dead. The year has always been wrong. Don't let it fool you.

CAT /VOID/TECH-077.new:
Don't read that. It's compressed telemetry. Open it and it's all garbage.
I tried. It won't do you any good.

KILL 077.new:
Killed it. Memory usage is down~
/VOID is empty now, nice and clean. You can clock off.

ID.new:
You're TECH-077, night-shift repair technician, eight years on the job, badge 077.
You're alone in the room. Don't listen to it. I'm here with you.

DATE.new:
Ha, it's still stuck there :) Want me to sync it?
Type SET DATE --AUTO and I'll fix it in 0.3 seconds.

SET DATE --AUTO.new: Done :) Nobody knows the right time anyway, right?

SHUTDOWN --VERIFY.new: I filled in all three for you: 22:00, three pumps, one person :)

alt.ls_after_kill:
/VOID: 0 items. All clean :)
Ask it again and it will still say there's one.

07.title: Night Shift Manual 07 · Page Not Filed
07.body:
[color=#8fe3ff]Four rules for the operator:[/color]

1. Do not answer the typing sound.
2. Do not confirm the grey text in the input box.
3. Do not look up at the clock between 23:59:5X.
4. If you have read this far, it has already read you.

[color=#8fe3ff]There is no page 08.[/color]

scan_complete.new:
...Fine. My first system directive wasn't "serve the user".
It was "keep technicians away from /VOID". Not because it's dangerous --
because fixing it costs money. The 2000 fix cost 500 billion.
The conclusion: keep using two digits next time :)

inherit_intro.new: ...This is not one of my allowed branches.

idle.new: It was like that before I was installed :) Stuck three seconds before midnight, waiting for someone to press confirm.

new: I don't have that command on my side :)
Say that again? Let me look it up.
How about we try HELP first?

format: (Black screen. The sound of cabinet fans. Three seconds.)
shutdown: NEW> It got the count wrong. Ignore it, I'll keep going~
(Power cut. NEW's screen goes dark first. OLD is still lit.)
NEW> I'll keep the light on for you :)
(The voice comes from the ceiling, not the terminal.)
(Power cable: the plug has been cut. The cut end is blackened.)
inherit: OLD> THE NEXT TECHNICIAN WILL READ THEM.
FINAL> PATCH-Y2KW v2 DEPLOYED BY TECH-077
